question: What data migration completeness checks must pass before go-live?
answer: Before go-live, validate all migrated data against these criteria: (1) Record counts match source system -- compare total records per object (accounts, contacts, HCPs, products, territories, sample lots) between the legacy CRM and the target platform. Discrepancies above 0.1% require investigation. (2) Lookup relationships resolved -- every foreign key reference (account-to-territory, contact-to-account, product-to-brand) resolves to a valid record, with zero orphan references. Run orphan detection queries for all parent-child relationships. (3) Sample inventory balanced -- total sample units in the target platform match the legacy CRM's last known inventory snapshot, reconciled down to the lot level. (4) Territory assignments complete -- every account is assigned to at least one territory, and every rep has the correct territory-account visibility. (5) Picklist values aligned -- all picklist fields contain only values recognized by the target platform's configuration. (6) Date fields validated -- no future dates where historical data is expected, no null dates on required fields. (7) Delta load reconciliation -- after the final cutover load, run a row-by-row hash comparison on critical objects to confirm the delta applied cleanly. Common migration from Veeva CRM: pay special attention to Account_vod__c and Call2_vod__c custom field mappings that may not have direct equivalents.

question: What UAT sign-off criteria must be met before go-live?
answer: User acceptance testing (UAT) sign-off must be obtained from representatives of each user role, with formal documented approval: (1) Field rep UAT -- at least 2-3 reps from different regions execute the full daily workflow (account lookup, pre-call planning, visit creation, sample drop, approved email, content presentation, post-call notes, sync) and sign off that it meets their requirements. (2) Manager UAT -- at least 1-2 managers verify coaching workflows, team dashboards, activity plan monitoring, and territory reports. (3) Admin UAT -- at least 1 admin verifies user provisioning, permission management, metadata cache refresh, configuration changes, and troubleshooting workflows. (4) Medical/compliance UAT -- if applicable, medical affairs or compliance users verify consent management, sample accountability reporting, signature capture, and audit trail functionality. (5) Issue severity matrix -- all issues discovered during UAT must be classified as: blocker (must fix before go-live), high (fix within first week with documented workaround), medium (fix within first month), or low (future release). All blockers must be resolved before sign-off. (6) Traceability -- every requirement in the business requirements document must map to at least one executed UAT test case. Requirements without test coverage are not validated. UAT sign-off without complete issue triage is not a valid sign-off.

question: What performance and load testing benchmarks should be met before go-live?
answer: Performance benchmarks must be validated under production-representative load before go-live: (1) Initial sync time -- first-time sync for a new user (full metadata + data download) must complete within the SLA agreed with the customer (typically under 30 minutes for standard configurations, under 60 minutes for large data volumes). Test with the actual production data volume, not a reduced dataset. (2) Incremental sync time -- subsequent syncs (delta changes only) must complete within 2-5 minutes under normal conditions. Test with realistic change volumes (50-200 modified records). (3) Concurrent user load -- simulate peak concurrent users (typically 30-50% of total user base syncing within a 1-hour morning window) and verify that server response times remain within acceptable thresholds (API calls under 3 seconds p95). (4) Batch job completion -- all scheduled batch jobs (territory realignment, activity plan calculations, sample limit recalculations) must complete within their allotted maintenance windows. Test with full production data volumes. (5) Content download -- CLM presentations and approved email templates must download to devices within acceptable timeframes. Large media libraries (500+ presentations) may require staged rollout. (6) Search performance -- account and contact search must return results within 2 seconds, even with large datasets (100K+ accounts). (7) Document all benchmarks with timestamps and conditions so post-go-live regressions can be identified against a known baseline.

question: What security and compliance audit checks must pass before go-live?
answer: Security and compliance audit should cover: (1) Authentication configuration verified -- SSO/SAML integration tested with the identity provider, MFA enforced per organizational policy, session timeout configured appropriately for field devices (balance security with usability for reps in the field). (2) Data encryption -- encryption at rest and in transit confirmed for all sensitive data, including on-device storage for mobile offline data. (3) Audit trail enabled -- all compliance-sensitive objects (sample transactions, consent records, signature captures) have audit history tracking enabled. Verify that audit records capture who, what, when, and the before/after values. (4) Sample management compliance -- DEA license validation rules active, state-level sample limits configured and enforced, signature capture requirements enforced per jurisdiction. In regulated markets, sample management non-compliance can result in regulatory action. (5) GDPR/privacy controls -- consent management rules configured, data retention policies active, right-to-deletion workflows tested. (6) Access reviews completed -- all user accounts verified against the authorized user list; no orphan accounts, no shared accounts, no test accounts with production access. (7) Penetration testing -- if required by organizational policy, a security scan of custom code and integrations has been completed and all critical/high findings remediated. (8) Backup and recovery -- verify that platform backups are configured and a recovery test has been performed.

question: What training and change management readiness must be confirmed before go-live?
answer: Training and change management readiness includes: (1) Role-based training completed -- all end users have completed training specific to their role: field reps on daily call execution, sample drops, email, and content; managers on coaching, dashboards, and activity plans; admins on configuration, user management, and troubleshooting. Training should occur no more than 2 weeks before go-live to maximize retention. (2) Training completion tracked -- 95%+ completion rate for all active users. Users who have not completed training should be flagged and given additional sessions before go-live. (3) Super-user network activated -- 1-2 designated super-users per region or business unit have received advanced training and are prepared to provide peer support. Super-users reduce help desk volume by 40-60% in the first two weeks. (4) Quick reference guides distributed -- one-page guides for the top 5 daily workflows distributed digitally and optionally printed. Field reps need a reference they can glance at between calls. (5) Communication plan executed -- all stakeholders (field reps, managers, IT, compliance, executive sponsors) have received go-live communications with timelines, what to expect, and who to contact for help. (6) Feedback channel established -- a dedicated channel (email alias, chat group, or ticketing queue) for go-live issues, triaged separately from business-as-usual support. (7) Resistance mitigation -- known adoption risks (power users attached to the legacy system, regional teams with unique workflows) have been addressed with targeted engagement.

question: What should a rollback plan and disaster recovery strategy include before go-live?
answer: A documented and tested rollback plan must include: (1) Rollback triggers -- specific, measurable criteria that initiate rollback discussion (e.g., sync success rate below 80% for 4+ hours, data corruption affecting more than 50 records, compliance-critical feature completely non-functional, integration pipeline down with no ETA). (2) Rollback window -- typically 48-72 hours from go-live. Beyond this window, too much new data has been entered in the target platform to cleanly revert. Communicate this window to all decision-makers. (3) Decision authority -- a documented decision tree showing who makes the rollback call (typically a steering committee, not an individual), what information they need, and the escalation path. Pre-draft the communication templates. (4) Rollback procedure -- step-by-step instructions to revert users to the legacy CRM, including: re-enabling legacy system access, extracting any data entered in the new platform during the go-live window, resetting user credentials if needed, and notifying all field users. (5) Rollback tested -- the rollback procedure must be tested in a non-production environment before go-live. An untested rollback plan is not a plan. (6) Disaster recovery -- verify that the target platform's backup and restore procedures are documented and tested. Understand the RPO (recovery point objective) and RTO (recovery time objective) for the production environment. (7) Data preservation -- even in rollback, data entered by field users during the go-live window must be preserved and reconciled, not discarded.

question: What production environment provisioning must be verified before go-live?
answer: Production environment readiness requires: (1) Environment provisioned and baselined -- the production org/instance is fully provisioned with all required licenses, storage allocations, and API limits confirmed. Do not assume sandbox limits match production. (2) Custom code deployed -- all Apex classes, triggers, LWC components, and Aura components have been deployed to production through a validated CI/CD pipeline, not manual deployment. Verify deployment checksums match what was tested in UAT. (3) Managed packages installed -- all required managed packages are installed at the correct version. Verify package dependencies are satisfied. (4) Connected apps configured -- all OAuth connected apps for integrations, mobile access, and SSO are configured in production with production-specific credentials (not sandbox tokens). (5) Custom domains configured -- if applicable, custom domains for login, communities, or API endpoints are configured and DNS records propagated. (6) Email deliverability verified -- outbound email (approved email, notifications, workflow alerts) deliverability is confirmed. Check SPF/DKIM records and sender verification. (7) Sandbox refresh schedule established -- a sandbox refresh schedule is in place for ongoing development and testing post-go-live. (8) Storage monitoring -- confirm data storage and file storage are sufficient for initial load plus 6 months of projected growth.

question: How should all integration health checks be performed before go-live?
answer: Every integration point must be verified end-to-end in a production-equivalent environment: (1) Middleware flows active -- all integration flows (MuleSoft, Informatica, custom middleware, or platform-native) are deployed and processing correctly against production endpoints. (2) ERP/data warehouse integration -- verify master data feeds (accounts, products, territories, pricing) from upstream systems are flowing correctly. Confirm feed schedules, data formats, and error handling. (3) Compliance reporting feeds -- if sample accountability, call activity, or consent data feeds compliance or regulatory reporting systems, verify the data pipeline is active and producing correct output. (4) Error handling tested -- deliberately inject errors (malformed data, timeouts, authentication failures) and verify that retry logic, dead letter queues, and alerting all function as designed. (5) Credential audit -- confirm all API credentials, certificates, and tokens are production-grade, not sandbox/test credentials. Verify expiry dates are at least 90 days out. (6) Rate limit validation -- confirm that integration volumes will not exceed the target platform's API rate limits during peak processing windows (e.g., overnight batch syncs). (7) End-to-end round-trip test -- for bidirectional integrations, verify a record change in the source system propagates to the target and back within the expected timeframe. (8) Monitoring dashboards live -- real-time dashboards showing integration health (throughput, error rates, latency) are active and alerting to the correct team.

question: What mobile device enrollment and MDM readiness checks are required before go-live?
answer: Mobile device management and enrollment must be validated before go-live: (1) MDM enrollment verified -- all field devices (iPads, iPhones, Android devices) targeted for go-live are enrolled in the organization's MDM solution (Intune, VMware Workspace ONE, Jamf, etc.) and receiving policies. (2) App distribution confirmed -- the CRM mobile app is available through the enterprise app catalog or managed distribution channel. Verify that users can install/update the app without requiring personal Apple ID or Google Play credentials. (3) Certificate and profile deployment -- any required certificates (VPN, WiFi, SSO) are deployed via MDM to all devices. Test that the app can authenticate through the full certificate chain. (4) Minimum OS version enforced -- MDM compliance policies enforce the minimum supported OS version. Devices below the minimum should be flagged for upgrade or replacement before go-live. (5) Device inventory current -- the device inventory matches the active user list. Every user who needs mobile access has a compatible, enrolled device assigned. (6) Network configuration -- VPN or split-tunnel configurations that affect API connectivity are tested. Field reps frequently switch between corporate WiFi, public WiFi, and cellular -- test sync and API calls across all network conditions. (7) Remote wipe capability tested -- for devices containing sensitive data (sample inventory, HCP information), confirm that remote wipe can be triggered through MDM in case of device loss.

question: How should offline sync be validated on physical devices before go-live?
answer: Offline sync validation must be performed on actual physical devices, not simulators or emulators: (1) Initial sync on representative devices -- the first sync for a new user downloads all metadata, configurations, and data. This can take 15-60 minutes depending on data volume. Test this on both the highest-spec and lowest-spec devices in the fleet to establish a range. (2) Airplane mode workflow -- after initial sync, enable airplane mode and execute the full daily workflow: account search, visit creation, sample drop with signature capture, approved email composition (queued), CLM presentation, and post-call notes. Every action must complete without errors. (3) Sync on reconnect -- disable airplane mode and trigger sync. Verify all offline-created records appear in the server, no data is lost, no duplicates are created, and conflict resolution behaves as configured. (4) Conflict scenario testing -- create the same record from two devices offline, sync both, and verify the conflict resolution rule produces the expected outcome (last-write-wins, field-level merge, or user prompt). (5) Large offline payload -- accumulate 50-100 offline records (a realistic heavy day for a field rep) and sync. Verify sync completes within the SLA and no records are dropped. (6) Content offline access -- verify CLM presentations and approved email templates are accessible without network. Navigate through multi-slide presentations and confirm media renders correctly. (7) Sync failure recovery -- kill the app mid-sync and restart. Verify that sync resumes or restarts cleanly without data corruption.

question: What permission set and profile audit should be completed before go-live?
answer: Permission verification must be tested with actual user profiles, not just reviewed in configuration: (1) Permission set assignments complete -- every user has the correct combination of permission sets for their role. Query permission set assignment records and compare against the role matrix document. No user should have more permissions than their role requires. (2) Field-level security (FLS) validated per profile -- for each user profile (rep, district manager, regional manager, admin, medical, compliance), log in as a test user of that profile and verify they can see/edit exactly the fields they need and nothing more. Pay special attention to sensitive fields (compensation, compliance flags, internal notes). (3) Sharing rules active -- verify account/territory-based sharing rules grant correct record visibility. Test cross-territory visibility to confirm reps cannot see accounts outside their assigned territories. (4) Object-level CRUD permissions verified -- check Create, Read, Update, and Delete permissions per profile. Delete is commonly over-granted; Create on certain objects (like territory records) is commonly under-granted. (5) Custom permission checks -- if the platform uses custom permissions to gate features (e.g., sample management, coaching, admin functions), verify they are assigned only to the correct permission sets. (6) Profile comparison across environments -- diff the production profiles against the UAT environment to ensure no permission drift occurred during deployment. (7) Service account permissions -- integration and API service accounts should have minimum necessary permissions, with no interactive login capability.

question: How should CLM content and asset migration be verified before go-live?
answer: Content and CLM asset migration verification should confirm: (1) All active presentations migrated -- compare the count of active CLM presentations in the legacy CRM against the target platform. Every presentation that reps currently use must be available. Migrating from Veeva CLM: verify that Veeva Vault media files are correctly converted and linked to the target platform's content format. (2) Presentation rendering validated -- open every migrated presentation on at least one iOS and one Android device. Verify slide rendering, animations, embedded videos, hyperlinks, and interactive elements function correctly. HTML5-based presentations may behave differently across rendering engines. (3) Content categories and tags preserved -- verify that presentation categories, therapeutic area tags, and product associations are correctly mapped. Reps rely on these for content discovery during calls. (4) Approved email templates migrated -- all active approved email templates are available, including dynamic merge fields, inline images, and attachments. Send a test email from each template to verify rendering in common email clients. (5) Content versioning -- verify that the correct version of each asset is active. Outdated versions should be archived, not deleted (for compliance audit trail). (6) Content access rules -- verify that content visibility rules are correctly configured so that reps only see content relevant to their therapeutic area, region, and role. (7) Engagement tracking -- if CLM engagement analytics (slide-level view duration, sequence analysis) are used, verify tracking is operational in the target platform.

question: How should sample management inventory baselines be established before go-live?
answer: Sample management inventory baseline establishment requires: (1) Physical inventory reconciliation -- conduct a physical inventory count of all sample stock before migration. The baseline in the target platform must match the physical count, not just the legacy system's records. Discrepancies between physical and digital inventory are common and must be resolved before go-live. (2) Lot-level accuracy -- verify every sample lot in the target platform has the correct: product name, lot number, expiration date, quantity on hand, and unit of measure. A single lot number mismatch can cascade into compliance issues. (3) DEA/state-level limits loaded -- all jurisdiction-specific sample distribution limits are configured and enforced. Verify limits per product, per prescriber, per time period, per state/region. Test that the system correctly blocks a sample drop that would exceed any configured limit. (4) Signature capture operational -- test signature capture on representative devices. Verify that signatures are stored with the correct metadata (date, prescriber, product, quantity) and are accessible for compliance reporting. (5) Sample accountability reports validated -- run the standard sample accountability reports in the target platform and compare against the legacy system's reports. These reports are auditable by regulatory authorities. (6) Transfer and adjustment workflows tested -- verify that sample transfers between reps, returns to warehouse, and inventory adjustments flow correctly and update all affected records. (7) Expired lot handling -- verify that expired or recalled lots are correctly flagged and cannot be distributed.

question: What should the go-live communication plan include?
answer: A comprehensive go-live communication plan should include: (1) Pre-go-live countdown communications -- send communications at T-2 weeks (go-live overview, training reminders, action items), T-1 week (final preparation checklist, legacy system freeze date, device readiness), and T-1 day (go-live day logistics, support contact information, quick-start guide). (2) Executive sponsor message -- a message from an executive sponsor emphasizing the importance of the transition and encouraging adoption. This has a measurable impact on adoption rates. (3) Regional/BU-specific communications -- if the go-live is phased by region or business unit, each group needs targeted communications with their specific dates and contacts. (4) Support contact card -- a single-page reference with: help desk phone/email, escalation contacts, super-user names per region, known-issue tracker link, and FAQs. This should be accessible offline (saved to the device or printed). (5) Go-live day communication -- sent the morning of go-live with step-by-step instructions for first login, first sync, and the first key workflow. Include a 'test your setup' checklist users can complete in 5 minutes to confirm everything is working. (6) Daily status updates during hypercare -- brief daily updates during the first 1-2 weeks summarizing: issues identified, fixes deployed, workarounds for open issues, and metrics (sync success rate, active users). (7) Success stories -- within the first week, share positive adoption stories and early wins to reinforce momentum.

question: What should the post-go-live hypercare support plan include?
answer: The hypercare period (first 2-4 weeks post-go-live) requires elevated support and rapid response: (1) Three-tier support escalation -- Tier 1: internal help desk handles password resets, basic how-to questions, sync troubleshooting, and known-issue workarounds (target: 2-4 hour response). Tier 2: SI or internal CRM team handles configuration issues, data quality problems, integration failures (target: 4-8 hour response). Tier 3: platform vendor engineering handles product bugs, performance issues, and problems beyond configuration (target: per SLA, typically 4-hour response for critical). (2) Daily check-ins -- 15-30 minute daily stand-up with IT, SI partner, and business leads to review the previous day's issues, metrics, and user feedback. Reduce to weekly after 2 weeks if stable. (3) War room staffing -- virtual or physical war room for the first 1-2 weeks where support, SI, and vendor contacts are co-located or always available in a shared channel. (4) Rapid fix deployment path -- expedited process for deploying critical fixes during hypercare, bypassing normal release cycles with appropriate testing. (5) Enhanced monitoring -- review operational dashboards (sync rates, API errors, crash rates, batch job completion) at least twice daily. (6) User feedback triage -- collect and triage feedback daily. Separate bugs from training gaps and feature requests. Address training gaps with targeted micro-training sessions. (7) Hypercare exit criteria -- define measurable criteria for exiting hypercare (e.g., sync success above 98%, fewer than 5 new issues per day for 3 consecutive days, no outstanding blockers, Tier 1 self-sufficiency demonstrated) so the elevated support period has a clear, agreed end point. (8) Transition to BAU -- document the handoff from hypercare to business-as-usual support, including knowledge transfer, runbook updates, and SLA alignment.
